topic: EMI is a pricing interface, not a payment option
selectedWhy: Recent cycles have covered AI operating-model lenses and an e-commerce returns-as-insurance mechanism. This cycle shifts to a different India-relevant lever: the EMI/BNPL widget at checkout. The non-obvious thesis is that EMI changes the unit of comparison from total price to monthly outflow, so checkout becomes a pricing interface (and an underwriting decision), with measurable impacts across growth, unit economics, and customer operations.
journalTitle: EMI Is a Pricing Interface, Not a Payment Option
linkedinDraft:
Your price tag is not ₹49,999.

It’s ₹2,999/month.

In India, EMI/BNPL isn’t just a way to pay. It’s increasingly the way the price is understood at the decision moment.

Once customers compare monthly outflow instead of total cost, checkout stops being a payments choice.
It becomes a pricing interface.

That framing shift edits the unit of comparison — and units matter more than we admit.
You’re no longer competing only on product vs product.
You’re competing against the customer’s monthly commitments.

And even when MRP doesn’t move, “no-cost EMI” still has a cost somewhere (fees, subvention, margin, promo budget).
If your discounting discipline only tracks coupons, you can miss the biggest leak: the checkout itself quietly becomes the discount.

A few practical implications:

- EMI changes valuation: customers ask “Can I live with ₹Y/month?” instead of “Is it worth ₹X?”
- EMI changes your funnel: it can lift conversion + AOV, but also shifts who you attract (and what support load follows).
- EMI is underwriting: defaults, tenure options, and which SKUs are financeable are strategy decisions.
- Measure the full loop: repeat rate, post-purchase friction (cancels/returns/disputes), and net margin after financing — not just conversion.

Full version here:
https://mohitsaikrishna.in/journal/emi-pricing-interface?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=emi_pricing_interface

If your checkout has EMI/BNPL, what decision is it really optimizing today: affordability, conversion, or brand trust?
